palette_source.description_used: earthy calm sage olive stone grounded natural

off_toolbox_moves: earthy-sage palette (not a common AI-blog palette)
serif body on a dev blog (most use sans-serif)

trends_extracted: warm color accents on clean background

name: vdua
philosophy: Building things, learning things, writing about it. A personal tech blog by vdua — notes on AI, AEM Forms, and system design, written for fellow engineers who want depth without pretension.

primary.name: Lichen
primary.use: page background (light mode), card surfaces, soft fills

primary.name: Sage
primary.use: tag pills, secondary CTAs, hover states, borders

primary.name: Moss
primary.use: links, primary CTA fill, anchor color, active states

primary.name: Loam
primary.use: body text, dark surfaces (dark mode background), footer

borderRadius.usage: Gentle rounding — not pill-shaped, not sharp. Calm and approachable.

patterns.name: Sage Outline
patterns.style: background: transparent; color: #52796F; border: 1.5px solid #84A98C; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 20px; font-weight: 500

motifs.name: Understory line
motifs.description: A thin 1px horizontal rule in Sage (#84A98C) at 30% opacity, used to separate sections. Evokes forest floor layering.
motifs.usage: Between article sections, before footer. Not between every element — only at major content boundaries.

motifs.name: Leaf mark
motifs.description: A small typographic ornament (§ or ❧) in Sage, used as a section break within articles instead of a horizontal rule.
motifs.usage: Within long articles to mark topic shifts. One per article maximum.

heading.usage: All headings h1–h4. Inter brings clarity and technical precision.

subheading.usage: Article metadata (date, reading time, tags), nav labels

body.usage: Article body text. Lora is a serif with good screen rendering — warm, readable, editorial without being stuffy.

accent.usage: Emphasis within prose, pull quotes. One italic accent per paragraph maximum.

eyebrow.usage: Category labels, tag headers, section eyebrows

rules: Heading scale: h1=2rem, h2=1.5rem, h3=1.25rem, h4=1.1rem
Code blocks use JetBrains Mono or Fira Code

photography.style: Not applicable — tech blog uses code blocks, diagrams, and screenshots. No stock photography.
rules: Diagrams should use the brand palette (Sage, Moss, Canopy)
Screenshots should be clean, focused, well-cropped
Architecture diagrams use simple box-and-arrow style
donts: No stock photography of people at keyboards
No generic tech imagery (circuit boards, abstract data flows)
No hero images — let the writing speak
photography.social: Use Canopy (#354F52) background with white text for OG images

voice.character: A thoughtful engineer sharing notes from the workbench. Clear, specific, honest about what they know and what they're still figuring out.

do.text: Here's what I learned building this, and where I got stuck.
The architecture looks simple on paper. In practice, three things broke.
do.context: Contrast between theory and practice — shows real experience

do.text: I'm not sure this is the right approach, but here's my reasoning.

dont.text: This revolutionary AI paradigm will disrupt everything!
Obviously, you should use microservices here.
In this blog post, I will discuss...

rules: Write like you're explaining to a smart colleague over coffee
Show your work — include code, configs, error messages
Admit uncertainty — 'I think' and 'in my experience' are fine
No em dashes — use commas, colons, or periods
No exclamation marks in technical prose

tone.description: Neutral-to-serious for technical content. Slightly warmer for retrospectives and learnings. Never playful, never cold.

writingGoals.description: Share practical knowledge from real projects — not theoretical, not tutorial-style, but 'here's what I found'
Create reference material for AEM Forms that others can use when they're stuck
Architecture retrospectives — what worked, what didn't, what I'd do differently

cleverVsClear.clever: Never. This is a technical blog, not a magazine.
cleverVsClear.clear: Always. Every sentence should be immediately parseable.

contentPillars.name: AI
contentPillars.description: Learnings from working with AI — models, tooling, practical applications. Not hype, not research papers, but engineering notes.

contentPillars.name: AEM Forms
contentPillars.description: Help articles and blog posts about Adobe Experience Manager Forms — solutions to real problems, configuration guides, best practices.

contentPillars.name: Architecture
contentPillars.description: System design learnings and retrospectives — what decisions were made, why, and how they played out.

personas.name: The Fellow Engineer
personas.description: A mid-to-senior engineer who found this article via a direct link, search, or colleague's recommendation. They want depth, specifics, and honesty.
personas.motto: Show me the code and tell me what broke.
